text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.

- The cabinet accepted the basic principles of a new pension system on Thursday. Among others, the cabinet also authorised the payment of surplus subsidies to the agricultural sector this year to the tune of 4.746 billion forints. @
- President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro of Italy and Hungarian President Arpad Goncz Thursday opened a new transformer factory owned by Ganz Ansaldo Rt. in Tapioszele.
- New Romanian Foreign Minister Adrian Severin accepted Thursday an invitation from his Hungarian counterpart to pay a visit to Budapest possibly before the end of the year.
- The International Court of Justice in the Hague will hear the arguments of Hungarian and Slovak delegations in litigation regarding the Gabcikovo hydroelectric power plant from March 3, 1997. @
- The central budget received revenues of 165 billion forints and disbursed some 200 billion in November, said deputy state secretary at the Finance Ministry Csaba Laszlo.

- Public train transport will cost 18 percent more, while goods transport will go up by 20 percent from January. Telephone tariffs will also go up by 20 percent. Water supply and sewerage will cost in Budapest 24 percent more, garbage removal 23.38 percent more and district heating 21.9 percent more. @
- Ikarus president Gabor Szeles signed an agreement on the delivery of 700 Ikarus buses to the Moscow company Moszgotransz on Wednesday.
- The National Savings Bank is to introduce a new loan scheme for individuals from December 16.
- The holding Graboplast Rt. is expected to close this year with pre-tax profits of 2.1 billion forints on consolidated sales of 22.5 billion forints.
- Hungarian Investment and Development Bank has received a $100 million syndicated loan from a consortium comprising 19 banks from 10 countries, led by Commerzbank AG. @

- Young Democrat President Viktor Orban has set March 1997 as the final date for opposition cohesion, saying that the next elections will be lost if opposition leaders do not rally together as soon as possible.
- The balance of foreign trade over the first ten months of 1996 showed a net deficit of $1.8 billion, said deputy state secretary at the Ministry of Industry and Trade Lajos Berenyi.
- The Government Supervisory Office has submitted its report to the government on the privatisation of Budapest Bank. @
- The insurance firm Hungaria Biztosito is expected to close this year with sales of 49.2 billion forints, 22 percent up on last year.
